cubes.text: The locker room hums with distant showers and the clang of metal doors. Mike pulls you past the last row of lockers, into a cramped nook where the light flickers and the air smells faintly of ammonia. He opens his bag, pulls out a small vial and a syringe, and fills it with calm precision. You watch, your pulse thumping in your throat. He glances at the entrance, then back at you.
Relax, man. Nobody comes back here. Here, this’ll kick in fast.
